html:
A South African Anglican archbishop and one of the best known opponents of apartheid. He trained as a teacher, then became a priest, and rose to be the first Black Anglican Bishop of Johannesburg in 1985 and Archbishop of Cape Town from 1986 to 1996.

As head of the South African Council of Churches from 1978, he called for nonviolent resistance and for foreign sanctions against South Africa, while many leaders of the African National Congress were in prison or exile. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984.

After apartheid ended he coined the phrase "Rainbow Nation". Nelson Mandela asked him to chair the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which from 1996 heard victims and gave amnesty to perpetrators who told the full truth. He was famous for weeping at its hearings and for his laughter. In later years he criticised corruption in the ANC government and spoke up for gay rights and for Palestinians.
